page: Microsoft Azure D4_v3 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the Dv3 family. It is powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2673 v4 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The instance features 4 dedicated vCPUs, which map to 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The CPU operates at a base speed of 2.3 GHz and includes a 50 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage is bundled with a local 102 GB SSD, and the instance runs on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

In terms of performance, the D4_v3 exhibits characteristics that position it in the lower tiers of modern cloud compute resources. Benchmark results indicate poor single-core and multi-core CPU performance, with stress-ng scores of 836.26 and 1943.87 respectively, both falling into the bottom 10% of tested servers. Memory bandwidth is also limited, with read-only large block operations measured at 19.2 GB/sec and write operations at 13.31 GB/sec, both categorized as poor. However, the instance achieves an average single-threaded gzip compression throughput of 24.35 GB/sec. Other tests, such as Geekbench software compiling and Passmark database operations, consistently place the instance in the bottom 10% to 25% performance brackets.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the D4_v3 offers a low-cost entry point for workloads requiring a dedicated CPU allocation and a balanced memory-to-core ratio, though it trades off raw processing speed and memory throughput. The bundled 102 GB local SSD provides basic storage without requiring external attachments. Given its performance profile, this instance is suited for low-demand workloads such as basic web serving, lightweight database operations, simple text processing, and development or testing environments that do not require high-performance computing or rapid memory access.
